archetype.name: Rebuilding (Zion-dependent)
archetype.definition: A third straight losing season is taking shape around one elite interior scorer and a young guard-center pairing. The defense is too porous to compete most nights, so the year is about development and lottery position rather than the standings.

report.headline: A 5-13 record that matches the margin, sinking with a bottom-two defense
report.take:
New Orleans is exactly as bad as its record says. At 5-13 with a W vs Pt Diff of 0, the margin implies the same 5 wins it has, so there is no bad-luck story to lean on. The Net Rtg of -8.1 sits 27th, the full-season pace points to roughly 23 wins, and the site has them 25th of 30. This is the third straight season in that neighborhood after 21-61 and 26-56, so the slide isn't new; it's the baseline.

The identity is unusual. The Pelicans take the fewest threes in the league (3PA Rate 34.7, 30th) and get to the line more than anyone (FT Rate 35.1, 1st). That is a Zion Williamson offense: he is 5th on the power forward tab with a 65.3 TS % and a +19.1 On-Off, and the frontcourt is the only group grading above a D. But the lack of spacing caps the ceiling. The eFG % of 51.4 is 29th, the ORtg of 112.2 is 20th, and outside Zion, Trey Murphy III and Jordan Poole, efficient scoring is scarce. Jeremiah Fears carries a 25.7 USG % at a 53.9 TS %, which is the price of a developing lead guard.

The defense is what sinks them. The DRtg of 120.3 ranks 29th, worse than last season's 118.9, and opponents finish at the rim at 70.3%, also 29th. Power forwards and centers feast: opposing PFs put up 6.41 more points, rebounds and assists than their own averages, 29th in the league. The month split tells it plainly. October was 2-4 but outscored opponents per game. November collapsed to 3-9 with 124.83 allowed a game, including 87-138 at Golden State and 111-145 to Brooklyn. One quirk stands out: Herbert Jones has a dreadful box line (44.2 TS %, -6.9 BPM) but a +23.2 On-Off, the best on the roster. Whatever stopping power this team has seems to come with him on the floor.

With Dejounte Murray out and both Zion and Murphy listed day-to-day, the near term depends on health. The last five games were at least competitive, a -5.8 margin a game against a 1-9 ten-game stretch, so there is a floor. But nothing in the profile says this team climbs toward the play-in. Expect a low-20s win total with the meaningful story being Fears, Derik Queen and Yves Missi.

strengths.title: League-best at drawing free throws
strengths.body: New Orleans gets to the line more than any team, a clear jump from last season's 28.4 FT Rate. It is the product of a rim-attacking, low-volume three-point attack built around Zion and Queen. It should hold as long as Zion plays, because it is a style rather than a shooting streak.

strengths.title: Zion is a genuine star engine
strengths.body: Williamson ranks 5th of 86 at his position, scores at a 65.3 TS % and leads the roster in Win Shares. The team is far better with him on the floor, which is why the frontcourt grades C+ while the other groups sit at D or D+. His health is the single biggest lever on this team's level.

concerns.title: Interior defense is near the bottom
concerns.body: Opponents shoot 70.3% at the rim, 29th, and the overall DRtg ranks 29th, worse than last year's already poor mark. Opposing power forwards and centers produce well above their norms. That points to a frontcourt that scores but doesn't protect the paint. Without a rim protector playing big minutes, this looks structural rather than a slump.

concerns.title: No spacing, poor shot-making
concerns.body: The lowest 3PA Rate in the league combined with a 33.6 3P % leaves the eFG % 29th. Defenses can pack the paint against a Zion-centric attack. Poole and Murphy are the efficient outlets, but Murphy has played only 10 games and Murray is out, so the guard shooting load falls on a rookie-level creator in Fears.

concerns.title: November collapse is real, not luck
concerns.body: The ten-game stretch went 1-9 at a -16.7 margin a game, and the W vs Pt Diff of 0 means close-game fortune isn't hiding a better team. The October scoring edge vanished as the offense dropped and the defense gave up 124.83 a game in November.

trend.note: A 2-4 October with a positive scoring margin gave way to a 3-9 November full of blowouts. The last five games tightened the margin, mainly because the defense allowed fewer points, but the record hasn't followed.

weekAhead.headline: Two winnable games bracket a hard Portland trip
weekAhead.body:
The week opens at home against Phoenix and then becomes a three-game road swing: the Clippers, Portland, and Sacramento the next night on a back-to-back. Two of the four opponents are as bad as or worse than New Orleans. The Clippers are 4-11 with a defense nearly as leaky (Opp eFG % 56.5, 28th), and Sacramento is 2-14 with the league's 29th-ranked ORtg. Those are the realistic wins, though the Clippers already beat them 139-123 earlier this month.

Phoenix and Portland are the tougher tests for different reasons. Phoenix is the worst defensive-rebounding team in the league and gives up big games to centers, a door for Queen and Missi. Portland is the bad matchup: an 8th-ranked defense that keeps opponents away from the rim and stops them there, which strikes right at how New Orleans scores. A 2-2 week would be a decent result; Zion and Murphy's day-to-day status decides whether that is the floor or the ceiling.

keyMatchups.title: Glass and centers against Phoenix
keyMatchups.body: Phoenix ranks last in DRB % and allows the most points and rebounds to opposing centers. New Orleans' bigs are its most reliable group, so this is the game to win on second chances and interior volume.

keyMatchups.title: Portland walls off the paint
keyMatchups.body: Portland ranks 8th in DRtg, 6th in Opp Rim FG % and 5th in keeping opponents away from the rim. That is the worst possible style for a team that takes the fewest threes in the league. It is the likeliest loss of the week.

keyMatchups.title: Sacramento's soft rim, second night
keyMatchups.body: Sacramento lets opponents shoot 75.7% at the rim, the worst in the league, though it limits how often they get there. Attacking the basket should pay off. The catch is tired legs on the second half of a back-to-back that ends a road trip.

weekAhead.watch: Whether Zion and Trey Murphy III are both on the floor: the offense has little efficiency without them.

restOfSeason.body:
Nothing in the profile points to a turnaround. The record matches the margin, the defense is 29th and slipping from last year, and the offense depends on one player's health and a free-throw-heavy style that can't fix the spacing. Some of November's worst blowouts will soften, since the recent five-game margin shows a team that is usually competitive. Murray's return would steady the backcourt. Our expectation is a final total of about 20 to 27 wins and a Net Rtg somewhere between -9 and -5.

The free-throw rate is sustainable and so, probably, is the rim defense problem. The upside case needs a healthy Zion playing most of the remaining games alongside Murphy, plus Jones' on-court defensive value showing up in a defense that climbs into the low 20s in DRtg. The downside is a Zion absence, which would strip the one A-level piece from a roster otherwise graded D.
swingFactors: Dejounte Murray's return and Murphy's health
Any improvement in rim protection from Missi and Queen

confidence.note: Only 18 games played, but the record and margin agree and the profile echoes last season.
